# Apply Fixes

## Change Summary

Added a `legacy_pre_stage_state_json` helper in `crates/tank_core/tests/save_load.rs` so schema v2/v3 migration tests build real pre-stage animal payloads and strip schema-6-only fields before migration. I also aligned the save-load reserve assertions with the current stage-cohort model by checking `AnimalState::total_reserve_g()` and the `animal.total_reserve_g` invariant. The weekly trim/export regression already used `animal.adult.count` and `animal.juvenile.count`, so it required validation rather than another code change.

## Steps

0. [Completed] Inspected the trim/export regression and confirmed it already uses the stage-cohort animal API in the current branch.
1. [Completed] Added a reusable legacy pre-stage save fixture helper and rewired the schema v2/v3 migration tests to use flat-animal payloads without schema-6-only fields.
2. [Completed] Updated save-load reserve expectations to use `AnimalState::total_reserve_g()` and the current `animal.total_reserve_g` invariant name.
3. [Completed] Ran the save-load regression suite and the targeted 500-hour trim-and-remove regression.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo test -p tank_core --test save_load` passed (21 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test save_load legacy_schema_v4_saves_migrate_trim_plants_to_trim_and_remove -- --exact` passed.
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking test_weekly_trim_and_remove_exports_nutrients_over_500_hours -- --exact` passed.

## Outstanding Risks

- I did not rerun the full `tank_core` test suite; validation covered `save_load` and the targeted 500-hour trim/export regression.
